record.paper_title: A General Framework for Coloring Problems: Old Results, New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For graphs of treewidth 2, what is the computational complexity of the radio coloring problem RC, where a radio coloring assigns positive integers to vertices so that adjacent vertices get labels differing by at least 2 and vertices at distance 2 get distinct labels, and the goal is to minimize the span, meaning the largest assigned label?

evidence.quote: The complexity of RC even for graphs of treewidth 2 is a long standing open question.
Recently Golovach proved that RC is NP-hard for graphs of treewidth 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A radio coloring (also known as an L(2,1)-labeling) of a simple finite undirected graph G=(V,E) is an assignment f: V → ℤ_{>0} of positive integers to the vertices such that:
  (i) |f(u) − f(v)| ≥ 2 whenever u and v are adjacent in G, and
  (ii) f(u) ≠ f(v) whenever u and v are at distance exactly 2 in G.
The span of f is max_{v ∈ V} f(v). The Radio Coloring problem (RC) asks, given a graph G and a positive integer k, whether G admits a radio coloring of span at most k.

A graph has treewidth at most 2 if it is a subgraph of a series-parallel graph (equivalently, it contains no K_4 minor).

Determine the computational complexity of the Radio Coloring problem RC restricted to the class of graphs of treewidth at most 2: is it polynomial-time solvable or NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved: P. A. Golovach proved that L(2,1)-labeling (equivalently, the Radio Coloring problem RC) is NP-complete on graphs of treewidth 2, separating tree (treewidth 1, polynomial) from treewidth 2. Related work by Fiala, Golovach, and Kratochvíl on distance-constrained labelings of graphs of bounded treewidth (ICALP 2005) provides the framework.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Complexity of Coloring Problems: Treewidth versus Vertex Cover
status_evidence.snippet: Golovach proved that the L(2,1)-labeling problem is NP-complete for graphs of treewidth two, thus adding a natural and well studied problem to the short list of problems whose computational complexity separates treewidth one from treewidth two.
status_evidence.claim: RC (L(2,1)-labeling) is NP-complete on treewidth-2 graphs, resolving the open question.

status_evidence.title: Distance Constrained Labelings of Graphs of Bounded Treewidth
status_evidence.snippet: Fiala, Golovach, Kratochvíl on distance-constrained labelings of graphs of bounded treewidth (ICALP 2005).
status_evidence.claim: Established hardness framework for distance-constrained labelings on bounded-treewidth graphs.
